messages:
maria: heads-up — canary for release v2.13.1 is spiking 500s on the /generate endpoint, started ~5m ago. seeing this on 2 of 5 canary hosts.

alex: copying logs — what percentage of traffic is on the canary?

maria: 2% traffic. canary auto-scaled to 5 instances during rollout. error rate jumped from 0.2% to ~18% for that cohort.

chris: i’m seeing a bunch of unexpected model load failures in the worker logs: 
```
ERROR model_loader: model load failed: digest mismatch for image redwood-registry/release:v2.13.1
expected: sha256:aa11bb22cc33\nfound: sha256:deadbeef0011
```
\nsam: that smells like retag/cross-push to me. did the CI push a new image to the same tag after prod signed manifest was generated?

maria: deploy-bot shows the build pipeline succeeded at 2435009000 and then a manual promote at 2435010200. i'm going to ping release eng.

deploy-bot: @eng-infra rolling canary to 5/5 hosts for v2.13.1 (image tag v2.13.1). rollout id: r-2026-03-15-0910.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — SEV2 — canary model load failures (route /generate). Paging: oncall-rotation.

oncall-rotation: i'm oncall, taking it. starting triage.

alex: quick customer-impact check — are any regions affected or just canary pool? stackdriver shows 500s originated from us-west-2 canary pool only so far. however a few downstream requests to the hosted API returned 502s about 2m ago (likely fallback).

chris: i pulled the image digests from the internal registry: 
```
$ curl -s https://registry.internal/v2/release/manifests/v2.13.1 | jq -r '.config.digest'
sha256:aa11bb22cc33
$ docker inspect redwood-registry/release:v2.13.1 | jq -r '.[0].RepoDigests[]'
redwood-registry/release@sha256:deadbeef0011
```
so the tag points at a different digest than the manifest recorded by our signing step.

sam: that confirms cache-poison/retag. that will break reproducible deploys — runtime tries to pull the signed manifest but the tag now resolves to a different blob.

maria: options: 1) kill-switch feature flag to stop the rollout (prevent more hosts from updating), 2) roll back canary to v2.13.0, 3) instruct registry to restore previous tag/digest if we have immutable snapshot, 4) revoke tag and require new signed release.

alex: we should avoid flipping registry tags if possible. faster: kill the rollout and roll back the canary to v2.13.0, then block traffic to the affected canary pool. i'll take kill-switch + rollback.

chris: i can run the rollback job now — triggering short lived rollback to image v2.13.0 on the 5 hosts.

deploy-bot: rollback job launched: job-id jb-9981. target hosts: canary-1..canary-5. estimated job time ~60s.

maria: i'm toggling feature flag `deploy.allow-canary-rollout` to OFF for env=production. doing it via console now.

maria: done — flag off. new deployments to canary groups will be blocked. :white_check_mark: 

alex: rollback status?

chris: job reporting 4/5 succeeded, canary-3 failed due to image pull error (same digest mismatch). hitting it with a manual docker pull and inspect.

chris: manual pull shows the registry returns header `X-Image-Source: external-proxy` for canary-3 attempt — looks like a replication/edge proxy pulled a different digest into the cache.

sam: we need to evict the proxy cache or block reads to that node. ask infra to flush the registry edge cache for canary-3 region. @eng-infra can we flush?

maria: paging registry team. pinging @registry-ops.

registry-ops (sam): ack, flushing edge cache for the key `release:v2.13.1` in us-west-2.

registry-ops (sam): flush done. verifying digest now.

chris: after flush, manual pull returns correct digest. re-running rollback on canary-3.

deploy-bot: rollback job jb-9981 updated: canary-3 requeued, progress 5/5 succeeded.

maria: observability — error rate back to baseline for canary cohort. no further 5xxs in the last 3 minutes.

alex: customer-impact assessment: small number of requests from hosted customers may have seen 500/502 for ~6 minutes. estimate: ~1200 requests, peak 0.01% of total traffic. no data leakage.

maria: opening incident in status page draft. initial severity SEV2 due to production error injection during release. adding timeline and mitigation steps.

sam: root cause candidate: retagging mutable tag after signing + replication edge cache divergence. mitigation actions: 1) enforce immutable tags for signed releases, 2) add registry replication checksums before promoting tag, 3) prevent manual promotes without signed manifest match, 4) improve canary isolation so partial pulls don't hit cached inconsistent images.

alex: also add automation: detect digest mismatch during node startup and avoid attempting to load models (fail fast with clear log) — we saw `digest mismatch` but some crashes cascaded.

maria: action items assigned: chris -> rollback automation and node failfast (P0), sam -> registry immutability policy + cache-evict API (P0), alex -> incident writeup and customer comms draft (P1), maria -> update runbook with kill-switch steps + add an explicit pre-promote digest check (P0).

incident-bot: incident logged: INC-2026-0315-001. responders: maria, alex, chris, sam.

maria: closing thread here for live mitigation — will keep the incident open and move to postmortem once RCA confirmed. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. :team-heart:

alex: nice work. follow-up: we should audit last 24h of tag operations to see if this was human error or CI glitch.

chris: creating a quick query against artifact events and will paste results in the incident doc.

sam: good catch. will follow up on registry hardening.

maria: logging final note for SEV2 timeline and immediate customer messaging: "Brief service errors observed for a small subset of requests during canary rollout; rollback completed and a registry policy will be implemented to prevent retagging. Working on a full RCA."

--- end of thread ---
